repo.description: ### Summary Dokploy 0.29.13 allows any authenticated member user to call `settings.getWebServerSettings` and receive the global web-server settings object. That object includes the stored `sshPrivateKey` value. The write endpoint for the same key is admin-only, but the read endpoint is only authenticated-user protected. In my proof, an owner stores an SSH private key through the normal admin-only mutation. A default member user cannot overwrite that key, but the same member user can read it back through `settings.getWebServerSettings`. ### Details The access-control boundary is inconsistent: - `settings.saveSSHPrivateKey` is an `adminProcedure`. - `settings.getWebServerSettings` is a `protectedProcedure`. - The returned settings object includes the `sshPrivateKey` field. Relevant source locations in Dokploy 0.29.13: - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/settings.ts:87`: `getWebServerSettings` is registered as `protectedProcedure`. - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/settings.ts:91`: the full settings object is returned. - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/settings.ts:303`: `saveSSHPrivateKey` is registered as `adminProcedure`. - `packages/server/src/db/schema/web-server-settings.ts:26`: `sshPrivateKey` is stored in the web-server settings table. This is not an unsafe custom integration issue. The proof uses Dokploy's built-in settings router and a normal default member role. ### PoC Use the attached PoC: - `poc/settings_ssh_private_key_disclosure_probe.py` Run: ```bash python poc/settings_ssh_private_key_disclosure_probe.py ``` The PoC uses a local Dokploy 0.29.13 instance and two normal authenticated sessions: - owner session - default member session The owner stores a private key through the admin-only endpoint. The member then attempts both write and read access. Observed result: ```text scope=Dokploy v0.29.13 official release image attacker_role=default member admin_only_key_save_status=200 member_key_save_status=401 member_key_save_denied=True member_settings_read_status=200 member_received_private_key=True received_private_key_sha256=4f7706cf9d1fda45ee1b5285fe50fece4aebe504c01e064572e59a8f8981b306 expected_private_key_sha256=4f7706cf9d1fda45ee1b5285fe50fece4aebe504c01e064572e59a8f8981b306 verdict=member_private_key_disclosure_confirmed ``` Expected result: The default member should not receive the stored SSH private key. The field should be omitted, redacted, or the endpoint should require admin permission. Actual result: The default member receives the same private key value that only an admin can write. ### Impact A default authenticated member can disclose the global SSH private key configured for Dokploy web-server operations. Depending on how the key is used, this may expose infrastructure access, deployment credentials, or server-management credentials. The demonstrated impact is high-confidentiality secret disclosure. ### Attachments - `poc/settings_ssh_private_key_disclosure_probe.py` - `evidence/evidence_run.txt` - `screenshots/settings_before.png` - `screenshots/settings_after.png` [settings_ssh_private_key_disclosure_probe.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30334166/settings_ssh_private_key_disclosure_probe.py) [evidence_run.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30334170/evidence_run.txt)
repo.summary: Dokploy member users can read the global web-server SSH private key through settings.getWebServerSettings
